doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Changes in jazz and advice to young players
title: Advice to young players on audience and the music business
summary: Young players call for advice; he urges them to choose an audience, understand digital income and make sure they get paid.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Interesting you say that because on my way home last night I had an NPR show on and they were playing this music and I couldn’t quite place it but then the person came on and they were doing a show about Indian music — music from India — and its effect on jazz and how some people embrace that. So you’re correct, there’s Celtic influences, in fact bands sometimes like to promote themselves as embracing world music so you have jazz and all these other influences coming in. When you mention about the number of players coming into the music, have you had people come to you, young players seeking advice about how to make a living in jazz?

Oh yeah, I do. I am, you know a lot of young players will call me up and talk, which I like, I like that. And they will ask for advice — musical advice — more often than not that kind of advice or saxophone advice. And then now and then business advice. And I will, you know, I will tell them the little I know and give them the best advice I can. And you know that’s a hard — I’m much better at giving musical advice or saxophone advice. Business advice, I need some advice myself on that. I’ve done things my way, I’ve gone my way, my particular way, and so each player of these young people, it’s very important to figure out what demographic they want to cater to in terms of the public, and these are the things I tell them about. You know jazz is — we talked earlier — is a pretty under the name of so-called jazz is a pretty big umbrella you know, and a variety of style and musical behavior by people and groups that will say “jazz.” So okay, so be it. So with that in mind I will tell — I give the advice to young people since it is that way then figure out who do you want to reach you know? Because there’s an audience for all of these different nuances and these different genres. There’s a straight-ahead bebop audience, or neo-bebop that leans towards that. I’m a member of that club. There are people that are more into more popular forms that have jazz as part of their DNA and then you have © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

rock, you have rhythm & blues, you have funk, you know you have all of these different takes on jazz music. And you’ve got people from all over the world that are playing that are bringing nuances of their culture to the music and amalgamating it with some of the part of the DNA of what I would say jazz is. So you have all that. So there’s a big audience and who do you want to reach. And then think about that deeply, because whatever — you want to do something that makes you happy, you want to do something that you do need to take care of yourself, you need shelter, you need — you know you’ve got to pay your rent, you’ve got to live and it takes money to live. Think about just the basic mundane problems of trying to play art in this society and music in particular, and jazz is really a pretty difficult sell. So you have to think about that and then think about what kind of music are you able to be honest about and play, and then think about the business aspect. I definitely tell them to learn all of the new ways that music is being used these days. So you’ve got all the digital, all of that, and then you know you’ve got cell phone, you’ve got streaming, you’ve got — there’s millions of dollars being made with music and so I will tell them to understand every aspect of the music business, not just playing in some bar you know, “I Got Rhythm” in some club, or “Countdown” in some joint, which is fine, I love that, but think about the ways that music generates money, and make sure that you get paid. Because there’s a lot of people that really make a lot of money off of music and by way of music and music is being played by people. Make sure that you get your just due. So that means you have to have some business awareness and understanding, and you’ve got to take part of your consciousness and your energy and really kind of look at these things. Now I will say this: a lot of the young players of today are a lot more on that page than I was as a younger person in my early twenties. You know I didn’t really think deeply about money, business, or anything. I just really wanted to learn how to play, and really play really well you know play as fast as possible.
